 When will UK storm end as heavy rain and 80mph gale-force winds batter Britain
 Holly Kintuka, Fionnula Hainey Updated 2026년 10월 25일 일 오후 8:14 UTC 1 Storm Boelo hit the UK this weekend. (Image: Getty) The UK is being battered by heavy rain and gale-force winds as Storm Boelo storms across the country, just after Storm Austen wreaked havoc for many. The first two named storms of the season hit in quick succession this week, leaving thousands of households in the south west without power and several areas facing severe flooding .
 While Storm Austen cleared to the east of England on Friday evening, Storm Boelo has drenched the UK with Brits having faced several hours of wet weather this weekend. Forecasters have previously warned that "damaging gusts" of up to 80mph are likely across the north of the UK, while it's unlikely that anywhere will be spared from the rain.
 On Friday, Storm Austen saw gusts of 76mph recorded at St Mary's Airport in the Isles of Scilly , while 74mph was recorded at Aberporth in south Wales and 71mph at Culdrose in Cornwall. Winds associated with Storm Boelo are likely to be even stronger, with an amber warning for wind covering much of Scotland, Northern Ireland and parts of the north of England.
 Chief forecaster for the Met Office Jason Kelly said on Friday: "Storm Boelo will be felt across the UK this weekend, with the strongest winds and greatest potential for disruption in the north. Amber warnings are in place across mainland Scotland , parts of Northern Ireland and the far north of England, where gusts of 60 to 70mph are expected widely, with the potential for 80mph in exposed coastal locations.
 "Strong winds will also affect other parts of the UK, with gusts of 50 to 60mph possible in places. Heavy rain will provide an additional hazard, particularly in the north, bringing the potential for further impacts. People should prepare for the potential for disruption, particularly to travel and power supplies. Secure loose items outside, plan ahead if you are travelling and keep up to date with the latest forecast and warnings for your area."
 The Environment Agency issued 22 alerts for spots across England where flooding is possible, as well as a warning that flooding is expected at New Brighton, Merseyside, because of high tides in the Irish Sea.
 Meanwhile, widespread travel disruption is expected to ferries and trains with TransPennine Express warning against all but essential train journeys on Saturday and Sunday, and Avanti West Coast strongly advising users not to travel north of Preston on Sunday, Manchester Evening News reported.
 Storm Boelo weather warnings remain in place until Sunday evening. An amber warning for wind and a yellow warning for wind remain in place until 9pm.
 The storm brought heavy rain. (Image: Getty) However, respite from the storm will likely be short-lived as the Met Office has warned that unsettled conditions are expected to continue into next week, particularly in the north, as another area of low pressure approaches the UK.
 The rain is set to return at the start of the week, with a large band of rain sweeping in from the south on Monday morning. The Met Office has also issued a wind warning for northern parts of the UK on Tuesday.
 Further ahead, there are signs of higher pressure becoming more influential towards the end of the week, which could bring a transition towards more settled conditions for parts of the UK, the Met Office said.
